analysis:
This PR changes only the CI threat-review scanner, not provider, runtime or coordinator code. No threat-model asset or boundary (TB-002/003/007/009/011, T-041 etc.) is directly affected.

1) Depth routing. The RISK/CRITICAL regexes moved from context.py (base 13-14) to the new depth_policy.py (head 6-7).
- path_depth now scores each file separately instead of matching one joined path string.
- .github/workflows/ files always go to Sol (head 14-15).
- docs/, changelog.d/, test trees and .md/.mdx/.rst files return None before the CRITICAL check (head 18-22). A test or doc path containing attest/crypt is no longer path-escalated; findings and needs_deeper_review still escalate it (head 37-40).
- Delimited test/spec filenames are checked only after CRITICAL (head 28), so AppAttest.swift-style names stay Sol.
- previous_filename is checked, so a rename cannot evade escalation (head 36).

2) budget_scan.py run().
- Base 330-331/337-338 sent every batch to depth review when integration produced findings or uncertainty. Head 358-365 instead targets only the batches cited by retained findings (finding_batches, head 329-337).
- Integration needs_deeper_review now only adds a manual_review_reason (head 366-370), which still forces human review.
- Non-forced runs drop Opus for batches already selected for Sol (head 374-375). Opus can still escalate to Sol at head 399-403.
- This reduces depth coverage for cross-file interactions whose uncited counterpart batch is never revisited. It is a deliberate cost/coverage policy, and human review is still required on uncertainty, so I do not treat it as a regression.

3) Added plan_calls (head 318-327) and the finished flag. Diagnostics now export finished plus bedrock_call_* keys (diagnostics.py head 82-83).

Unverified (outside the supplied source):
- Whether any other module or test still imports context.RISK or CRITICAL; the removal would cause an ImportError.
- plan_calls assigns paid.last_request without a hasattr guard; the native adapter is assumed to support it.
- The bedrock_* snapshot values come from paid.metrics(), which is not shown. Confirm they are content-free numbers or enums before they reach the public diagnostics artifact.

None of these is evidenced as a vulnerability.
